page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.3xlarge is a compute-focused instance from the Enhanced family, built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. It allocates 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 24.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions feature AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI), and cryptographic accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady mid-tier execution across general computing and vector-heavy operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1530.0 and a multi-core score of 7429.0, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 16374.15 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 11659.32. Cryptographic performance reflects hardware acceleration support, recording 10956.36 in the PassMark encryption suite. Memory throughput reaches 641.24 GB/sec for small cached blocks, though it tapers to 36.2 GB/sec during uncached 256 MB reads. In inference tests, small model prompt processing reached 1081.58 tokens per second, but 7B model prompt handling settled in the bottom tier at 24.2 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure design perspective, the instance relies entirely on remote networked block devices, featuring 0 GB of local storage, and incorporates an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete hardware accelerators, with a GPU count of zero. Given its 1:2 memory configuration and dedicated core allocation, the hardware provides cost-effective compute density for CPU-bound pipelines without the overhead of excess memory allocation. Tradeoffs include modest large-block memory read bandwidth and the lack of included local disks, which requires consideration for persistent I/O workloads.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.3xlarge is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration and software build pipelines, batch data processing, API backends, web serving clusters, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference tasks.

It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs (6 physical cores, 2 threads per core), 24.0 GB of RAM, and 48 MB of L3 cache, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Instruction support includes AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. The server does not bundle local disk storage and lacks discrete GPUs, relying on an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show average mid-tier throughput, recording 16374.15 in PassMark CPU, 7429.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 16.68 GB/sec in static web serving, with weaker performance in uncached large-block memory reads. It serves as an efficient compute configuration for CI/CD builds, batch computing, API layers, and web servers.
